title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to ensure that AI tools used in veteran services are designed, deployed, and monitored responsibly, protecting veterans’ privacy, safety, and fairness. It establishes guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and accountability standards to prevent misuse and harm from AI applications in the veteran context.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is designed to improve national security by setting up guidelines for assessing and reducing risks from advanced AI systems. It encourages cooperation between government and industry to create secure AI deployments and promotes research into defensive technologies that protect against misuse.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 aims to address and reduce bias in algorithmic decision‑making tools and systems. It requires companies to assess, mitigate, and report on potential discriminatory impacts in AI products.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a policy that makes open‑source AI a national priority, encouraging agencies and companies to develop, share, and collaborate on AI models, data, and tools openly. It sets standards for transparency, ethical use, and collaboration, aiming to boost innovation and ensure that AI advancements benefit society as a whole.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to protect AI models from unauthorized copying and theft. It establishes legal penalties and enforcement mechanisms to deter individuals and organizations from illegally accessing or redistributing protected AI models.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 seeks to limit the use of artificial intelligence in medical practice, ensuring that human doctors remain central to patient care. It sets legal boundaries for AI involvement, protecting patient trust and professional accountability.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies to evaluate how their automated systems impact fairness, bias, and safety, and to take steps to mitigate any adverse effects. It mandates that these companies document their assessments, share findings with regulators, and provide clear information to the public about how the algorithms operate.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes standards for ensuring the reliability and safety of artificial‑intelligence systems used in defense. It requires detailed reporting on performance, risks, and compliance to promote accountability and transparency in military AI deployment.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed piece of legislation designed to promote the safe, fair, and transparent use of artificial intelligence. It aims to establish oversight, accountability, and regulatory standards for AI development and deployment.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a law that requires regular reporting on the development, deployment, and impact of artificial intelligence within China. It aims to give the government oversight over AI capabilities and ensure that AI systems operate within national standards and policies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to shield elections from the harmful effects of AI-generated misinformation. It seeks to regulate or restrict the use of deceptive AI in political messaging and campaign materials, ensuring voters are not misled by fabricated or misleading content.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a law designed to oversee the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems that can learn and modify themselves. It requires ongoing monitoring, regular reporting, and independent audits to ensure these systems operate safely, transparently, and within regulatory limits.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building new AI data centers to address environmental and energy concerns. It aims to evaluate the impact of AI infrastructure on climate and resource consumption before allowing further expansion.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising expenses caused by the energy consumption of large AI data centers. It proposes regulations or measures to curb the high energy costs associated with AI infrastructure that could otherwise impact families’ electricity bills.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to halt or restrict the construction or operation of new data centers specifically designed to support artificial intelligence workloads. The law aims to address environmental concerns, such as high energy consumption and carbon emissions, by limiting AI-driven data center expansion until more sustainable solutions are in place.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed legislative framework designed to regulate artificial intelligence technologies in the United States. It focuses on ensuring AI transparency, safety, and accountability while fostering innovation and protecting public interests.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets strict safety and privacy standards for AI-powered toys intended for children, requiring manufacturers to ensure that these toys do not expose kids to harmful content or data misuse. It mandates rigorous testing, clear labeling of data collection practices, and ongoing oversight to protect children’s safety and well‑being while interacting with AI‑enabled playthings.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to protect the privacy of minors who use AI technologies. It sets guidelines for how companies can collect, use, and share data about children and young people, ensuring that their information is handled responsibly.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act likely requires the government to produce a comprehensive report on the country’s AI development, capabilities, and strategic significance. It would set up oversight, data sharing, and policy guidelines to ensure China maintains a competitive edge and safeguards national security in the AI sector.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law aimed at regulating how AI models are built, used, and overseen. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and safety in the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill establishes rules that require developers of artificial‑intelligence systems to provide detailed functional bills of materials, explaining the components, algorithms, and dependencies that make up the AI product. It also includes additional provisions for oversight and transparency, so that regulators and stakeholders can audit and understand the AI’s design and operation.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act seeks to develop a skilled workforce that can responsibly design, deploy, and maintain artificial intelligence systems. By investing in education, training, and certification programs, the act aims to build public confidence and ensure AI technology is used ethically and safely.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is designed to regulate the environmental footprint of AI technologies, requiring companies to assess and report on their energy use, carbon emissions, and resource consumption. The law also establishes standards, reporting requirements, and incentives to encourage more sustainable AI development and deployment.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a bill that aims to curb unfair pricing in AI services and prevent employers from colluding to keep wages low. It proposes regulations and penalties for companies that overcharge customers or engage in wage‑fixing schemes in the AI sector.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes rules for using artificial intelligence in the agriculture industry, aiming to protect farmers, workers, and consumers. It sets standards for how data is handled, how algorithms are tested and documented, and how farms can safely adopt AI tools.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is designed to encourage banks, fintechs, and other financial institutions to adopt and develop new AI technologies. It balances this push for innovation with safeguards that protect consumers, secure data, and maintain the overall stability of the financial system.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to stimulate the adoption of artificial intelligence across banking, insurance, and investment firms by providing clear regulatory guidance and incentives. It establishes a sandbox framework and data access provisions to accelerate responsible AI solutions while protecting consumer privacy and market integrity.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This act aims to build and keep a skilled AI workforce by encouraging education, training, and partnerships between universities, businesses, and government. It also seeks to boost innovation by funding research, promoting diversity, and addressing ethical concerns in AI development.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act bans the creation or operation of artificial‑intelligence data centers on U.S. federal property, aiming to protect federal lands from the environmental and energy demands of large computing facilities. This measure is intended to preserve national land resources and limit the federal government’s role in hosting high‑energy AI infrastructure.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to incorporate AI education into primary and secondary school curricula, ensuring students understand artificial intelligence technologies, their uses, and potential impacts. It mandates the development of standardized AI literacy programs, teacher training, and resources to prepare students for an AI‑driven society.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed artificial intelligence education into elementary, middle, and high school programs, so students can develop a foundational understanding of how AI works and how it affects society. The law will also establish guidelines for teacher training, curriculum materials, and assessment tools to ensure that schools are prepared to deliver this new content effectively.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to set rules for how artificial intelligence can be developed and used, focusing on safety, fairness, and transparency. It introduces classifications of AI systems by risk level, requires companies to disclose AI usage and ensure human oversight, and establishes penalties for non‑compliance.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act aims to clarify how artificial intelligence can be integrated into educational settings. It sets guidelines for teachers, students, and institutions to use AI responsibly while ensuring transparency and protecting student privacy.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives is urging that anyone in America and any community affected by an AI data center’s construction or operation must be entitled to clear, open information about the center. This bill aims to give those communities a say in how the center is built and run, ensuring local control and transparency.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: This act is designed to stop AI systems from fabricating or promoting false claims of exploitation. It establishes safeguards, reporting obligations, and penalties to ensure that such deceptive uses are identified and prevented.
